hook: Ride a Ferris wheel and your height draws a sine wave. Drag the car or the graph and the other follows, so radius, hub height, speed and boarding point become amplitude, midline, period and phase.
outcome: Model periodic motion with a sinusoid, reading amplitude, midline, period and phase from a wheel; see radians as arc length on the unit circle and check that sin squared plus cos squared equals 1
sources: Wikipedia, Ferris Wheel (1893): height 80.4 m (264 ft), 36 cars, up to 60 people each, nine-minute nonstop rotation, opened June 21, 1893: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_Wheel_(1893)
Guinness World Records, First Ferris wheel: 80 m (264 ft) tall, 76 m (250 ft) diameter: https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/first-ferris-wheel/
JSTOR Daily, The Big Wheel: 250 feet in diameter (second source for the 1893 diameter, checked 2026-10-25): https://daily.jstor.org/the-big-wheel/
Wikipedia, London Eye: 135 m tall, 120 m diameter, 32 capsules, about 30 minutes per turn, public opening March 2000: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Eye

Wikipedia, Singapore Flyer: 165 m tall, 150 m diameter, 28 capsules, public rides from February 14, 2008, officially opened April 15, 2008, ride about 32 minutes: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore_Flyer

Wikipedia, High Roller (Ferris wheel): 167.6 m (550 ft) tall, 158.5 m (520 ft) diameter, 28 cabins, about 30 minutes per turn, opened March 31, 2014: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Roller_(Ferris_wheel)
